title: Wi-Fi Connected but No Internet
next: Next Friday: My Phone Battery Dies Too Fast
description: Full Wi-Fi bars but nothing will load? Kip and Bub explain why that happens and walk through the fixes, from restarting your router the right way to checking for an outage.

scenes.say: Your phone shows full Wi-Fi bars, but nothing will load. How can you be connected, and still have no internet?
It's Fix It Friday. Today: Wi-Fi connected, but no internet.

Here's the secret. Wi-Fi is just the link between your device and your router. The router gets the internet from your provider through a cable. If that part breaks, your Wi-Fi still works, but there's nothing on the other end.
First, find out how big the problem is. Do other devices have internet? If only one device is stuck, the problem is that device. If everything is down, it's the router or your provider.

card.title: One device or all of them?

scenes.say: The fix that works most often: restart your router and modem. Unplug them, wait thirty seconds, and plug them back in. Then give them two or three minutes to fully start up before you test again.

card.title: Restart the router the right way

scenes.say: If it's just one device, turn its Wi-Fi off and back on, or restart it. Still stuck? Tell the device to forget the network, then join it again with the Wi-Fi password.
One more clue: the lights on your modem. A red or blinking light often means it isn't getting a signal from your provider.

card.sub: It may not be getting a signal

scenes.say: If nothing works, it may be an outage. Check your provider's app or website using your phone's mobile data, or give them a call. Sometimes the problem is on their end, and all you can do is wait.

card.sub: Check your provider's app on mobile data

scenes.say: So: figure out if it's one device or all of them, restart the router the right way, rejoin the network, check the modem lights, and check for an outage.
